players.product: SMR designer - Doosan Enerbility forging/material supplier and prospective module manufacturer

quarterly_data.signal: Revenue of $0.1 million for the three months ended June 30, 2026, versus $8.1 million in the same period last year; the year-on-year decrease reflects the completion in late 2025 of the Fluor front-end engineering design Phase 2 work in support of the RoPower project, which had no comparable activity in the current quarter. Management expects both product and services revenue to grow as project activity advances.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue $0.1M in Q2 2026 vs $8.1M a year earlier

quarterly_data.signal: Closed Q2 with approximately $1.9 billion in cash, cash equivalents and investments, an increase of $900 million since March 31, 2026; investments alone moved up to $800 million versus the prior quarter as treasury shifted into longer-term high-grade instruments. CFO framed the liquidity as capital for supply-chain agreements and commercial readiness rather than start-up runway.
quarterly_data.figure: ~$1.9B cash, cash equivalents and investments; +$900M since 03-31-2026; investments $800M

quarterly_data.signal: Supply chain status: NuScale has assembled a network of more than 60 specialized suppliers covering fuel, safety and instrumentation and controls, valves, cranes and module handling, and has already negotiated supplier agreements with more than half of those 60-plus supplier relationships. Each supplier holds detailed design responsibility for its own scope with NuScale acting as technology systems integrator and engineer of record.
quarterly_data.figure: 60+ suppliers; supplier agreements signed with more than half

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: 'We have 12 modules of which a lot of them are currently in production, which are long lead items, and we've been working on those over a 2-year period.' The real long-lead items are the forgings, which have been in production for the last 2 years.
quarterly_data.figure: 12 modules with long-lead items in production; forgings in production for 2 years

quarterly_data.signal: Doosan Enerbility is NuScale's strategic partner on the major components of the modules - the heavy forgings at the heart of every NuScale power module. Slides showed photographs taken at Doosan's facilities in South Korea of actual components in active production for NuScale power modules.

Fuel: NuScale entered a dedicated agreement with Framatome to complete the fuel design ahead of any signed customer contract, because fuel design lead time is years not months; the fuel will be manufactured in the state of Washington. NuScale operates on standard low-enriched uranium available today from established suppliers, avoiding the HALEU supply dependency of competing designs.

This quarter NuScale announced that Paragon has been awarded a contract to complete the final design development of the safety instrumentation and control systems for the NuScale power modules; management said that work is ahead of schedule. Comparable relationships exist across cranes, module handling and valves, with additional announcements expected.

Commercial catalyst: strategic partner ENTRA1 Energy continues to advance discussions with the Tennessee Valley Authority toward a definitive power purchase agreement for potentially the largest nuclear power deployment program in U.S. history using NuScale SMR technology. Management said talks are active and progressing and that once PPAs are definitized NuScale will start the construction and operating license application, start front-end engineering design and initiate OEM contract negotiations.

RoPower (Doicesti, Romania) will deploy 6 NuScale power modules at a former coal plant site and is the most advanced SMR effort in Europe. NuScale is a subcontractor to prime contractor Fluor and completed the front-end engineering design Phase 1; the project now moves into pre-EPC leading to final notice to proceed roughly another year from now, pending the incoming Romanian government. Asked whether RoPower could trigger revenue-generating services in 2026, the CEO said 'if we get the contract in place, yes, there will be revenue next year.'
quarterly_data.figure: 6 NuScale power modules; final notice to proceed ~1 year away

quarterly_data.signal: Demand: 'We continue dialogue with hyperscalers, data centers... Texas just came out and stated here today that they have to shut down data center promotions because of lack of energy and water. We're an answer to that.' Management is in regular discussions with hyperscalers, utilities and governments, and cited the emergency planning zone approval plus dry cooling with air condensers as distinctives for siting next to end users.

Regulatory: NuScale remains the only SMR company to have received design certification from the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission, including standard design approvals for 2 of its designs. About 60% of the combined construction and operating license application (COLA) work done for the prior CFPP project can be carried over to the next U.S. project, and starting the COLA with the customer is the first initiative once PPAs are in place.
quarterly_data.figure: standard design approvals for 2 designs; ~60% of the COLA reusable

quarterly_data.signal: Cost structure: as an OEM, 'about 30 -- maybe 30-plus percent is going to be our cost and then the rest is going to be the EPC and other contractors.' Some strategic suppliers are also investors in NuScale and are pricing for sustainable multi-project supply rather than a one-off, which management says keeps rates competitive.
quarterly_data.figure: NuScale ~30%+ of plant cost; remainder EPC and other contractors

quarterly_data.signal: Operating expense discipline: CFO noted that over the past 10 quarters, from the beginning of 2024 through the end of 2025, OpEx was held within roughly a $2 million to $3 million band between about $41 million and $44 million per quarter; Q2 2026 OpEx was within about $1 million of Q1 after RoPower engineers moved from cost of goods sold into OpEx. No formal guidance given.
quarterly_data.figure: OpEx ~$41M-$44M per quarter over the past 10 quarters; Q2 within ~$1M of Q1
